desks.title: Course build — Data Storytelling for Analysts
desks.description: Designing a six-week cohort course: learning outcomes, the week-by-week plan and workload, the capstone and its rubric, and what's left to record before enrolment opens.
desks.brief:
## Course build — Data Storytelling for Analysts

**Format** 6-week cohort · 5 video modules · 3 live sessions · capstone project
**Enrolment opens** @+14d · **Cohort starts** @+35d · **Seats** 30
**Who it's for** analysts who can build the chart but lose the room when they present it

### Learning outcomes
By the end, a learner can:
1. State the one decision their analysis supports, in a sentence
2. Choose and declutter a chart for that decision
3. Structure a five-minute data story for a senior audience
4. Take critique and revise a draft in a single pass

### Design rules
- No week over 150 minutes of learner time
- Videos cut into segments under 12 minutes
- Every concept gets an exercise in the same week

### Where it stands
Three of five video modules recorded. The week-by-week load is uneven — see the callout. **Recording finishes @+10d so the trailer and sales page are ready when enrolment opens.**

callout.title: Weeks 2 and 5 break the 150-minute rule
callout.body: Week 5 carries 160 min because the capstone draft lands there; week 2 is 155. Fix: move the reading to week 3, pull a 30-min capstone outline into week 4 and trim the chart swap to 40. Weeks 2–5 then land at 150, 130, 135 and 130.

children.label: Fallback dataset for anyone without one

blocks.p: Four criteria, one per learning outcome, each scored 1–4. A pass needs **3 or more on every criterion** — not an average, so a strong chart can't carry a missing decision. Anything below 3 comes back with written feedback and one resubmit.
**4** — one sentence, a named decision-maker, a clear ask. **2** — a topic rather than a decision.
**4** — the chart type fits the comparison, and nothing on it goes unused by the story. **2** — default formatting, with the legend doing the work.
**4** — context, tension, answer and ask inside five minutes. **2** — walks through the analysis in the order it was done.
**4** — feedback from the peer review of the draft is visibly acted on. **2** — the same deck in new colours.

notes.title: Waitlist — what they told us
notes.body:
Asked the 212 people on the waitlist one question: what goes wrong when you present data?

Most common answers, in order:
- 'They ask a question I wasn't ready for'
- 'Too many charts, no point'
- 'I run out of time before the recommendation'

The third is why structure gets its own week, and why the capstone has a hard five-minute limit.

Thirty seats means about 14% of the waitlist has to enrol to sell out before the cohort starts.

desks.title: Cohort 7 live — SQL for Product Managers
desks.description: Week 4 of 6 with fourteen learners: who's on track, who's gone quiet, where the cohort is stuck, and the run sheet for this week's live session.
desks.brief:
## SQL for Product Managers — Cohort 7

**Week** 4 of 6 · **Learners** 14 · **Live session** weekly, 75 min, next @+2d
**Average progress** 58% · on pace would be 67% by the end of this week

### This week
- Module 4: joins, and why your numbers double
- Lab 3 feedback back to everyone by @+1d
- Live session 4: bring a query from your own job

### Who needs a nudge
Eight learners are on track. Three are a lab behind, two have gone quiet for six days or more, and Jolene has paused to defer to Cohort 8. Three quiet days triggers the LMS reminder email; six means a personal message and a 1:1 offer.

**The two quiet ones get a personal message today — another reminder email won't do it.**

callout.title: Gustavo and Lerato: quiet for 6+ days
callout.body: Both submitted lab 1 and stalled on lab 2, which is taking most people 90 minutes, not the 45 planned. Offer each a 20-minute 1:1 before the live session @+2d instead of another reminder.

children.label: Draw the tables before writing SQL
Live walkthrough of a bad join
Trim lab 4 to the core query

ol: 18:00 Welcome and wins from lab 3 (5 min)
18:05 The doubling join — live walkthrough of what goes wrong (15 min)
18:20 Breakouts in threes: fix a broken query (20 min)
18:40 Hot seat: two learners share a query from work (20 min)
19:00 Lab 4 brief and what 'done' looks like (10 min)

blocks.p: Freya and Daniyar have said yes. Ask Noor too — she's a lab behind, but her forum question this week was the best one anyone asked.

ul: Breakouts pre-assigned: mix on-track learners with those behind
Jolene stays enrolled but off the reminder list

notes.title: Lab 3 — feedback themes
notes.body:
Eight in, six marked so far:

- Four used SELECT * and then filtered in a spreadsheet
- Three forgot to GROUP BY the second column
- Freya's query is the cleanest — ask if it can be the model answer

Feedback to all eight by @+1d.

3. Ask Noor about the hot seat
